summary.short: EU Regulation establishing uniform requirements for ICT risk management, major ICT-related incident reporting, digital operational resilience testing and ICT third-party risk for listed EU financial entities, with a simplified regime for certain smaller entities.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 sets uniform requirements for the security of network and information systems supporting the business processes of financial entities. Article 2(1) covers listed entities, including credit institutions, payment institutions, investment firms, central counterparties, insurers and ICT third-party service providers. Chapter II requires a management-body-approved ICT risk management framework covering identification, protection, detection, response and recovery, with simplified rules for listed small entities under Article 16. Chapter III requires an ICT-related incident management process, classification of incidents, and reporting of major ICT-related incidents to competent authorities, with clients informed where their financial interests are affected. Chapter IV requires a digital operational resilience testing programme for entities other than microenterprises, and threat-led penetration testing at least every three years for entities identified by competent authorities. Chapter V sets principles for ICT third-party risk, including a register of contractual arrangements, exit strategies and contract termination circumstances. This annotation covers Articles 1 to 28 only; the application date is not in the text provided.

notes: Part 1 of 2: recitals and Articles 1 to 28 (Chapters I to V, Section I). Operative amendments to the five amended Regulations, critical ICT third-party provider designation and oversight (Art. 31 onward) and the Article 46 competent authority provisions fall in part 2, so amendment relations here rest on the title and recital 102. Empty strings stand for null (no registry ID, LEI or ticker in the text). Internal inconsistency: Art. 3(53) defines a small institution for occupational retirement provision as one with 'less than 100 members in total', while recital 42 says 'not more than 100 members'. Recitals also cite Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Regulation (EU) 2018/1725, Directive (EU) 2016/1148 and Europol; these appear only in recitals and are not recorded as relations. Part 2 of 2 (Arts 29-64, footnotes). Targets outside the registry have an empty target_instrument_id (schema requires a string) and the name in target_text. lei and ticker are empty strings for the same reason. Art. 46 designations under sector acts are coded as designates_under, except where the same act is amended here; that row notes it. Art. 58 review clauses name possible future changes to Directive 2006/43/EC and PSD2 oversight; these are coded as cross-references, not amendments. No internal inconsistency found in this part. Spot-check (Claude Opus, 2026-10-14): Art. 54(6) five-year publication limit runs from publication of each penalty decision, not of the Regulation, so no date is computed; removed the duplicate external 'published' row (the OJ citation in the text gives 27.12.2022); Art. 53 notification concerns Chapter VII, not Chapter V; ICT third-party service providers recoded from enterprise to cloud_service_provider (closest role); retention and publication periods (Arts. 54(6), 56(2)) removed from thresholds; added the delegated Art. 18(3) materiality threshold.

evidence.quote: By 17 January 2028, the Commission shall, after consulting the ESAs and the ESRB, as appropriate, carry out a review
